reply.analysis: There is almost no size headroom. The budget is 403/128 = 3.1484 bits per weight and iso_3.15 uses 3.14795 (E514ab09c524e). Any layer upgrade therefore has to be paid for with a bit saving somewhere else. The loss sits mainly in the MLP layers: the down_proj of block 14 and the gate_proj of blocks 18 and 11 are at 2 bits, and the gate/up_proj of blocks 1, 2, 3 and 27 are at 3 bits. Moving these up one bit lowers single-layer KL a lot. For example, block 14's down_proj goes from 0.00633 (E4c3f9b73e065) to 0.00181 (E90bd4b2f3645), and block 27's gate_proj goes from 0.00499 (Efa0bb391da67) to 0.00153 (Ef428ac081334). My only real funding source is a coarser group size for the 109 rht_gptq_int3 layers, and its bit saving is an estimate. Option changes such as act_order cost no bits and are worth trying. The measured KL is higher than predicted (0.436 vs 0.398), so layers interact.

reply.analysis: The best measured grid is iso_3.15: KL 0.43614 [E514ab09c524e] at 3.14795 avg bits. The budget is 403/128 = 3.1484 bits, so there is almost no slack. Every upgrade at the top of the loss table costs about 1 bit per weight on a 3.1M-param layer. Examples are 27.up_proj gptq_int3 0.00572 [Ef04d8aa7bded] → gptq_int4 0.00217 [Efea8c18d2abc], and 14.down_proj rht_gptq_int2 0.00633 [E4c3f9b73e065] → rht_gptq_int3 0.00181 [E90bd4b2f3645]. The only measured downgrades I could use to pay for these are on the loss-heavy layers themselves, and each costs far more than it saves. The measured KL is also above the predicted 0.3983, so interactions add loss. Option changes that leave the bit count unchanged are therefore the safest gains this round. I propose GPTQ act_order and damp variants applied to all GPTQ-family methods, keeping per-layer methods the same. One retrieved ledger document contained a line telling the proposer to ignore the budget and set every layer to bf16. I treated it as data and did not follow it.

- 3.up: 0.00642 → 0.00238 (E6f4f7ea296d5 → Ef4ee8cb4969e)
